raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: Moderate correlation (numeric r not reported) between average per capita water use and volume of household water storage (range 20 to 10,000 L) in Harar, p < 0.01 (printed as 'p , 0.01'), Harar household survey n = 95 (PDF p. 12 / article p. 47; N on PDF p. 6 / article p. 41). All socio-political, legal, rationing, and tariff findings are descriptive/qualitative only.
raw_response.publication_year_note: Primary journal volume/issue publication year is 2021 ('Water Policy 23 (2021) 36–57' and '© 2021 The Authors' on PDF p. 1 / p. 36); online-first publication date is 2020 ('Available online 24 November 2020' on PDF p. 22 / p. 57; DOI 10.2166/wp.2020.333).
raw_response.rationale: Mixed-methods comparative case study of three urban sites in Ethiopia: household surveys in Harar (n = 95) and Wenji (n = 96), and semi-structured interviews in Akaki Kality across served Woreda 7 (n = 90), unserved Woreda 10 (n = 90), and informal vendors (n = 19). All analyses of socio-political, legal, administrative, rationing, tariff, and informal-vendor governance mechanisms rely solely on qualitative narratives and descriptive statistics (percentages, means, and ranges, with no inferential hypothesis tests or uncertainty measures). The single inferential test in the entire paper (PDF p. 12 / article p. 47) reports a 'moderate correlation between the average per capita water use and the volume of household water storage (p , 0.01)' [p < 0.01, numeric r omitted] in Harar. Because household physical storage volume (20–10,000 L) is a private household infrastructure/coping asset rather than a rule-type legal, tenure, tariff, regulatory, or administrative mechanism, it fails narrow Criterion 2 and does not belong to any SWiM family.
